title: The Last Telegraph
subtitle: A Novel
author: Walusimbi Leon
description: In 1942, a young wireless operator in a coastal East African port intercepts a coded message that could change the course of the war — and a forbidden love with the woman who delivers the cables.
style: Period, atmospheric, close third-person. Detailed sensory prose; the hum of valves, the salt of the harbor, the weight of unsaid words.
characters: Yusuf — 24, wireless operator, quiet and watchful; Amina — telegraph clerk, sharp, wary, secretly literate in three languages.
setting: A British-administered port on the Indian Ocean, 1942.
notes: Open with Yusuf on the night shift. Establish the monotony, the war's distant rumor, then the anomalous message. Build slow-burning tension between duty and the woman at the counter.
